Gross margin unchanged from prior guidance: high-30s to low-40s% for the first generation (Q4 FY2027 and FY2028), targeting 50% over the next couple of years by bringing in-house work previously done by an ASIC partner. The AGI CPU is a 128-core design; more cores is 'clearly the direction of travel' for agentic workloads. Silicon revenue will be broken out as a THIRD reporting line (separate from licensing and royalty) once it exceeds 10% of revenue — expected in FY2028, with first shipments at the end of calendar 2026.

quarterly_data.signal: Supply chain is the binding constraint on the AGI CPU ramp, not demand: 'It is a very tight market across everything. Whether it's memory, whether it's test equipment, whether it's substrates, whether it's TSMC wafers' — Rene Haas noting even CPU rivals with their own fabs 'have not been able to supply the demand'. Confidence improved across ALL of wafers, substrates, test capacity and memory over the past 90 days, and management sees no single-point-of-failure component risk. Relief is expected as capacity expands into calendar 2028-2029 (FY2029-FY2030), where wafer and memory capacity estimates are up ~70-100%.
quarterly_data.figure: wafers/substrates/test/memory all tight; capacity +70-100% by CY2028-29

quarterly_data.signal: TAM reframing: Arm's March view of a $100B+ data-center CPU market (up from a $50-60B consensus at the time) now looks conservative — peers have since cited numbers up to $200B+, with the most recent estimate around $220B. Arm is NOT changing its published numbers (the $15B AGI CPU / FY2031 framework stands) but flagged the same market share against a $200B+ TAM would imply material upside; internal targets are higher than external. Driver: inference-based compute running agentic workloads is throughput-constrained by CPU count, so rising inference and agentic demand converts directly into CPU demand.
quarterly_data.figure: DC CPU TAM $100B (Mar) -> ~$220B external estimates; Arm numbers unchanged

quarterly_data.signal: Royalty mix shift — cloud AI is offsetting a weaker smartphone market. Higher memory prices are inflating handset BOM and OEMs are raising prices; the drag has broadened from the low end to 'all parts of the market, even some upper and mid-tier'. FY2027 royalty growth expectation trimmed from ~20% to 'closer to the high teens', with Q2 royalty guided to 13%; Arm still projects double-digit smartphone royalty growth despite a double-digit decline in the smartphone market, because most customers have moved to Armv9 and CSS (higher royalty rates). Licensing was raised to compensate, leaving the combined business ahead of plan. Management reaffirmed 20%+ royalty growth for FY2028-FY2029 as memory-driven handset weakness laps.
quarterly_data.figure: FY27 royalty growth ~20% -> high teens; Q2 royalty +13%; 20%+ reaffirmed FY28-29

quarterly_data.signal: Ecosystem and edge: Arm's software ecosystem now supports MORE THAN 22 MILLION developers. Introduced Performix (backed by Microsoft, MongoDB, Redis and SAP) to help developers and AI agents analyze and optimize workloads on Arm infrastructure, and the Arm MCP Server has passed 10,000 Docker downloads. Beyond the data center, NVIDIA's RTX Spark is the first agentic PC built on Arm compute subsystems, Windows on Arm expands via Snapdragon AI PCs, and physical AI (ADAS, robotics, Jetson Thor) contributed to royalty growth. On open-source/low-cost models management is 'net neutral to net positive' — agents need CPUs regardless of the model, and smaller efficient models would favor Arm's edge footprint.

Internal InP output capacity doubles YoY by the end of the current quarter, ONE QUARTER AHEAD of the original plan, and is on track to MORE THAN DOUBLE AGAIN by the end of calendar 2027; substrates and other critical inputs for that ramp are already secured, and capacity beyond 2027 is being planned. Concrete measure: Coherent produced about 80% MORE indium phosphide lasers in the June quarter than a year earlier — those lasers feed 800G and 1.6T transceiver shipments in the current quarter, so management expects data-center revenue growth this quarter to EXCEED 80% YoY. Six-inch lines in TEXAS and SWEDEN are producing EMLs, CW lasers and photodiodes with yields that exceed the 3-inch lines across all three device types; a third 6-inch location in ZURICH starts in the first half of calendar 2027. quarterly_data.signal: Financing: CoreWeave raised approximately $18 BILLION in Q2 across debt, convertibles and equity, including its inaugural Eurobond and its first ever delayed-draw term loan backed by HPC infrastructure issued in the public markets. Management called this strategically important because enterprises typically want two- or three-year rather than five-year contracts, so financing shorter durations opens whole new markets at higher ASPs and margins. Total debt and equity capital secured to date exceeds $32 BILLION, the weighted average cost of debt has fallen almost 300 basis points over the past year (about $1.1 billion of annualized interest savings on the end-Q2 debt load), and cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities exceeded $6.9 billion at June 30.

Timeline: 2026 = major qualification year (first customer aiming June/July, second end-Q3/Q4), production capability set up late 2026, MAINSTREAM VOLUME PRODUCTION 2027. TAM rule of thumb intact: ~150 HB systems for logic implies ~600 for HBM (a 16-high stack needs 16 bonds vs 1 for logic; each 2.5D module carries 3-4 stacks). For HBM high-volume production the integrated configuration (with Applied Materials Kinex automated lines) is the likely choice vs standalone for logic flexibility - bonder value to BESI is the same either way. JEDEC's possible 20-high stack height relaxation (775 -> 825/900um) does NOT change HB economics (only one of the three needs the extra height); interconnect yields must prove >99.9% (already 99.99%+ in logic HB).

quarterly_data.signal: THREE-TIER DEAL MODEL made explicit. (1) MID-TERM core AI cloud contracts of one to three years — four landmark deals closed in Q2 with REFLECTION, COHERE, an unnamed scale U.S. Neolab and a large U.S.-based quant trading firm, averaging MORE THAN $1B EACH at a yield of $20-25M PER MEGAWATT, upfront payments covering 50-60% of associated capex and payback under two years. (2) SHORT-DURATION capacity of up to six months for time-boxed needs (large training runs before a model release, RL post-training sprints) on dedicated GB300 clusters, being negotiated at $40-50M PER MEGAWATT 'and sometimes above' — roughly double the mid-term yield; one such deal signed recently. (3) LONG-TERM contracts with investment-grade customers, used primarily to finance the build-out. Management states it COULD SELL ITS ENTIRE 2027 CAPACITY TODAY on mid-term terms but is deliberately choosing NOT TO, retaining capacity for higher-value short-term demand; it has also tactically shortened how far in advance it sells, selling closer to deployment to improve realized pricing.

quarterly_data.signal: FIRST CAPACITY AUCTION as a price-discovery mechanism: it cleared at the highest price Nebius has ever seen for the BLACKWELL generation — 15% ABOVE THE HIGHEST PRICE IT HAD EVER CHARGED and 20% ABOVE its Blackwell pipeline pricing. Management framed it as letting the market set price directly in an environment where 'competitor pricing, analyst opinions, and even prediction markets are all over the place' and 'we have several buyers for every GPU'; the winning bidder plans to participate in future rounds. Both the auction and the short-term scale-training deals remain take-or-pay, use only a small portion of total capacity, and have faster close-to-deployment cycles. On competitive entry (xAI selling compute at premium prices), CEO Arkady Volozh said new entrants 'validate the market' — the AI cloud market is growing tens of gigawatts per year while Nebius plans roughly 1 GW per year, so hyperscalers 'cannot build all of it'.
quarterly_data.figure: first auction cleared 15% above highest price ever charged, 20% above Blackwell pipeline

quarterly_data.signal: CPO / ultra-high-power lasers: lead CPO customers' production plans 'remain very much on track, and their demand signal has increased since our last update.' Lumentum remains confident in an ultra-high-power laser chip demand ramp in the second half of calendar 2027, ahead of customer scale-up deployments in calendar 2028. Because the first phase of scale-up optical connections spans across compute racks within a cluster, the ramp applies to any topology larger than one rack. Ultra-high-power laser revenue is expected to reach roughly the $50 million mark by the end of calendar 2026, with the first triple-digit ($100M+) quarter expected in fiscal Q3 FY2027.
quarterly_data.figure: UHP laser ramp H2 CY2027 for CY2028 scale-up; ~$50M by end CY2026; first $100M+ quarter fiscal Q3 FY2027

quarterly_data.signal: First external light source (ELS) MODULE purchase order received, for delivery by the second half of calendar 2027 - Lumentum's first move up the stack from selling laser chips into selling the full ELS module. ASP is 'meaningfully higher than the set of lasers that we ship in'; module margins are above corporate average but below the laser chips, a deliberate trade of some margin for revenue acceleration. Wupen Yuen: the ELS module is positioned to enable 'customers who don't know how to deal with individual laser chips' to build CPO and NPO systems.
quarterly_data.figure: first ELS module purchase order (delivery H2 CY2027); ASP meaningfully higher than laser set

quarterly_data.signal: NPO (near-packaged optics) called 'completely additive' and 'significantly increasing the optical TAM.' The rest of the customer base beyond the lead CPO account is prioritizing NPO as an intermediate step to eventual CPO adoption; even the largest CPO customer is evaluating NPO for specific new use cases. Two laser types are being evaluated for NPO: a mid-power laser integrated directly into the optical engine, and a high-power laser in an external light source module. Lumentum's NPO/CPO laser family spans 120 mW, 150 mW, and 400 mW output levels off common design and process know-how. Wupen Yuen: each NPO set carries ~6.4T of bandwidth, roughly four times a local module, and NPO should hit the market in the late 2027 / 2028 timeframe to enable optical scale-up.
quarterly_data.figure: NPO additive to optical TAM; 120/150/400 mW laser family; ~6.4T per NPO set; market late 2027-2028

quarterly_data.signal: Supply-demand imbalance update: no change on EMLs (still shipping behind customer demand, previously cited at greater than 30%), but high-powered lasers have deteriorated sharply - 'we are way behind in our shipments... The demand signal has increased, and we are very much further behind relative to our ability to supply.' Management clarified the ramp execution itself is on track; the gap widened because demand accelerated. High-powered lasers were named as the one vector that materially changed since the prior quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: EML imbalance unchanged (>30%); high-power laser shortfall materially worse on accelerating demand

quarterly_data.signal: EMLs delivered another record-breaking quarter, primarily driven by 100G-per-lane devices. 200G EMLs are accelerating and now account for over 25% of total EML revenue; management expects 200G EMLs to be 50% or more of volume by mid-calendar-2027. Lumentum remains on track to deliver over 50% EML unit growth in the December 2026 quarter versus the year-ago quarter, but expects to remain significantly behind demand even at year end.
quarterly_data.figure: record EML quarter; 200G EML >25% of EML revenue; >50% EML unit growth by Dec-2026 quarter

quarterly_data.signal: CW laser strategy expanded materially. The new 200G-per-lane CW laser chip has a significantly reduced die size, is more efficient, and delivers margins accretive to long-term financial targets; Lumentum is commanding a significant price premium versus market price because tight spec width produces superior transceiver yields at customers. The margin gap between CW and EML 'has closed considerably' since the prior call (EML still better). Better-than-expected output in Japan is being allocated to CW, and Lumentum is now shipping CW lasers in a relatively meaningful way into the 200G-per-lane silicon photonics opportunity, on top of internal deployment in its own transceivers.
quarterly_data.figure: 200G CW laser: smaller die, price premium, margin gap to EML closed considerably

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: expanding across the two indium phosphide wafer fabs in Japan to capture coming 200G and 300G lane-speed opportunities, qualifying both CW and EML process flows on the newest tools as they come online. Demand for both EML and CW lasers is expected to grow significantly through the second half of calendar 2026 and into 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: two Japan InP fabs expanding; CW and EML flows qualifying on new tools

quarterly_data.signal: Pump lasers: shipments surged more than 80% year-over-year and Lumentum will 'remain effectively sold out for the foreseeable future despite our rapid capacity expansion.' A fourfold increase in pump laser shipments is still expected over the next several quarters. Share is roughly 70%-80%. Capacity is ramping at Rose Orchard (US) with packaging and test in Thailand. Multiple long-term customer agreements have been secured to help offset planned capital expenditures - mostly three-year arrangements with built-in pricing levers and, in most instances, take-or-pay structures, formed largely with NEMs (network equipment manufacturers).
quarterly_data.figure: pump lasers +80% YoY; 4x shipment increase expected; ~70-80% share; 3-year take-or-pay LTAs

quarterly_data.signal: Narrow linewidth laser assembly shipments grew sequentially for the 10th consecutive quarter and were up over 130% year-over-year. Scale-across demand is being driven by inferencing and training applications requiring full-rate connectivity between data centers, plus political and regulatory constraints favoring smaller, more modular builds. Scale of the DCI opportunity: for one major hyperscaler, the network capacity connecting just two AI data center sites is double the total global backbone capacity that hyperscaler built over the entirety of the last decade.
quarterly_data.figure: narrow linewidth +130% YoY, 10th consecutive sequential growth quarter

quarterly_data.signal: Cloud transceivers: record 800G shipments in the quarter while initiating production of next-generation 1.6T modules. Transceiver profitability continues to improve on yield gains, capacity utilization, and the initial rollout of higher-ASP 1.6T units. 1.6T uptake is expected to intensify starting in fiscal Q1 FY2027 and sustain through calendar 2027, anchored by lead Tier 1 hyperscale customers rolling out custom AI clusters. Management believes Lumentum is first to market ahead of larger competitors in many instances and can hold that share advantage through the cycle, crediting its signal integrity team on difficult 1.6T designs.
quarterly_data.figure: record 800G shipments; 1.6T production initiated; 1.6T uptake intensifies from fiscal Q1 FY2027

Tracking to (not ahead of) the previously stated $400 million of OCS shipments for the second half of calendar 2026, leaving room to run in the fourth calendar quarter. Demand signal for 2027 'continues to be incredibly strong'; initial work started to add capacity with contract manufacturers alongside increasing internal factory output. Lumentum describes itself as the only merchant OCS supplier with a shipping track record, and expects to cross over to become the number one OCS supplier sometime in early 2027 versus one customer's internal source of supply.
quarterly_data.figure: OCS shipments 2x QoQ; first $100M+ OCS quarter guided; $400M H2 CY2026 on track; #1 supplier expected early 2027

quarterly_data.figure: OCS in-tray and higher/lower port-count products; additive TAM; 2028 timeframe

No change to schedule - first revenue in early 2028, ramping through calendar 2028 to full pitch by end of 2028 and into 2029. Capacity remains uncommitted and Lumentum is actively talking to customers about laser demand, expecting to announce new Greensboro arrangements (LTAs) over the next couple of quarters.
quarterly_data.figure: Greensboro GaAs-to-InP conversion underway; first revenue early 2028; ramp into 2029; LTAs in discussion

quarterly_data.signal: InP substrate supply: after a surge in ultra-high-power laser demand across a couple of customers, Lumentum spent the last three months securing additional substrate supply and signed a deal with AXT during the quarter. Hurlston: 'we went out and we found additional substrate help from AXT. They are a great partner.' Lumentum is comfortable near-term on the strength of its lead arrangement with a Japanese supplier plus the AXT deal, but flagged that given the rate of change in the demand vector 'that may not be true a quarter or two from now either' - more substrate help is likely needed if the vector continues.
quarterly_data.figure: AXT InP substrate deal signed in Q4; more substrate supply likely needed if demand vector continues

quarterly_data.signal: Technology roadmap view: silicon photonics is a viable solution at 1.6T and CW lasers are taking a significant portion of transceiver output, but at 3.2T silicon photonics 'loses some of its advantages' and Lumentum expects EMLs to come back in a meaningful way. Wupen Yuen added that in a supply-constrained environment customers will use whichever laser source they can get, so the EML-versus-CW mix is a supply/demand dynamic as much as a technical one. CPO remains the natural end state - optics placed directly on the substrate or interposer for maximum power efficiency through foundry-level advanced packaging.
quarterly_data.figure: SiPho viable at 1.6T; EML expected to return at 3.2T; CPO the end state via foundry advanced packaging

quarterly_data.signal: Competitive: on Chinese companies bringing new indium phosphide fabs to market, Hurlston said 'we obviously haven't seen any impact on our numbers as yet. I don't expect there to be any impact,' citing EML differentiation, high/mid-power laser differentiation for NPO and CPO, and an ability to price up even in CW because tight spec consistency drives superior customer transceiver yields. He cautioned that some Chinese laser suppliers are not yet delivering into the market.
quarterly_data.figure: no impact seen from new Chinese InP fabs; price premium sustained

quarterly_data.signal: Adjacent businesses: industrial lasers and cable access strengthened quarter-over-quarter. Within industrial lasers, increased adoption of ultrafast lasers targeting high-density PCB via drilling that supports advanced AI XPU boards and 1.6T optical modules. In 3D sensing, Lumentum has visibility to an expanding set of applications expected to drive growth in upcoming product cycles with its primary customer.
quarterly_data.figure: ultrafast lasers for AI XPU board / 1.6T module PCB via drilling; expanding 3D sensing pipeline

quarterly_data.signal: Named by AOI management on its Q2 FY2026 call as one of the very few suppliers able to serve the high-power CPO laser market: AOI, Lumentum, Coherent and Broadcom are all 'invest[ing] huge money' in laser capacity, yet 'even combined... it's still very tough to meet the customer demand in the next few years'. Sizing: CPO/ELSFP needs a 300mW laser (vs 70mW for 800G, 100mW for 1.6T) with ~6x larger die, so the industry laser market must grow 8-10x; DWDM ELSFP carries 40-50% worse yield loss than 1310nm, and laser equipment takes 21-24 months from order to high-volume output. AOI states only AOI, Lumentum and Coherent can hit acceptable DWDM CPO laser / CPO module yields.

H1 revenue NT$444 hundred million, up 32% YoY from NT$335 hundred million (DRAM, NAND flash, eSSD and logic all up); H1 gross margin 20.6% (+4.3 points), net profit NT$52 hundred million - the Q2 profit of NT$28.5 hundred million alone nearly equalled all of last year's H1 - and H1 EPS NT$5.5 vs NT$2.88, up about 91%.

quarterly_data.signal: Memory market: AI servers keep driving HBM demand and high-end memory packaging demand stays very strong; DRAM and NAND market demand and prices are rising together, with customers maximising output of committed capacity - customer revenue gains are mostly price-driven as supply is limited, but PTI's packaging volumes are still growing and utilisation keeps improving. Packaging material costs keep rising and PTI is passing them through to customers gradually (its customers are large long-term partners, so price adjustments are made carefully each quarter). AI-server eSSD demand keeps rising with shipments expanding QoQ and YoY.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Fan-out panel-level packaging (FOPLP) for AI: chairman confirms PTI is an AMD AI-chip supply-chain partner providing fan-out PLP solutions and is actively pursuing more AMD AI-chip applications; despite equipment-delivery delays, installation issues and doing new-product qualification in parallel, the program is on schedule and PTI is confident of volume production before the middle of next year, which would make it the world's first company to mass-produce fan-out PLP for AI applications. The former-AUO fab conversion is going smoothly: floor 1 for middle-end/RDL processing, floor 2 for chip-on-panel and mounting packages onto ABF substrates; the G7 panel equipment supporting the AMD program is fully installed and in qualification, with automation being added. PTI showed an engineering sample of a 5x-reticle-size AI package (one reticle = 26x33mm) - it says only TSMC otherwise has this capability - and notes a G7 panel fits about 45 such large AI packages versus 8 to 9 on a wafer, positioning panel output as a complement to foundry wafer-based advanced packaging. FOPLP equipment lead times run about a year plus installation; management estimates a new entrant would need roughly three years from ordering to customer qualification (PTI started fan-out panel work in 2015). In high-end flip-chip BGA, PTI already mass-produces large FC-BGA/MCM and will move a large one-reticle-size chip package into volume production in Q3.
quarterly_data.figure: AMD fan-out PLP volume production before mid-2027 (target: world's first FOPLP for AI); 5x reticle-size panel packages, ~45 per G7 panel vs 8-9 per wafer; FOPLP equipment lead time ~1 year

quarterly_data.signal: Optical/CPO roadmap: the Broadcom cooperation has brought PTI into optical communications - it will build Optical Engines using its panel fan-out technology, with small-volume production of the first OBO and OSFP versions starting around end-2026; integrating the Optical Engine into a switch (a CPO switch) is targeted to start shipping in H2 2027, and integration of the Optical Engine into AI chips is expected around 2028 or later once designs mature (engineering simulations already completed). Separately, TSV interconnection for DRAM co-developed with a partner has completed DDR-5 trial production and moves to volume production and shipments in Q4 2026 - a foundation for future HBM manufacturing that management expects to start shifting DRAM packaging from 30-year-old wire-bond formats toward advanced packaging, with a meaningful revenue and margin contribution from next year.
quarterly_data.figure: Optical Engine small-volume production from end-2026 (OBO, OSFP); CPO switch shipments from H2 2027; AI-chip integration ~2028; TSV-based DDR-5 DRAM volume production from Q4 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 FY2026 revenue was JPY 62.02 billion, beating the forecast, and full-year revenue exceeded the previous forecast by JPY 5.1 billion, adjusted operating income by JPY 3.2 billion and adjusted net income by JPY 2.3 billion - although full-year revenue decreased 2% year-on-year and adjusted operating profit decreased 18%, on lower China DRAM equipment sales and upfront R&D/SG&A investment. Service revenue grew 27% year-on-year to 40% of total sales as upgrade modifications (mainly DRAM) replaced some new-equipment demand. Full-year equipment sales for NAND increased 90% and for DRAM 44%, while logic foundry decreased 11%. Annual dividend set at JPY 37; a share buyback of up to JPY 5.3 billion was resolved, and net cash of JPY 6.6 billion was achieved one year earlier than expected.

quarterly_data.signal: FY March 2027 guidance: revenue +19% year-on-year, adjusted operating profit +27%, adjusted net income +26%, with gross profit margin of 42%; annual dividend forecast JPY 47. Under the new classification (upgrade modifications, 200mm and used equipment moved from service into the equipment business), DRAM-related sales are expected to increase 36% year-on-year, logic foundry sales 38%, and NAND sales 7%; non-China equipment sales +39% while China equipment sales dip 3%, and the ratio of high-value-added products reaches 71%. The CY2026 WFE outlook was raised to 15% growth (up roughly 5 percentage points from the 10%+ view at Q3) on stronger AI-related investment; by application NAND +15%, DRAM +25% - +30%, logic foundry and others +5% - +10%; China -5%, non-China +20%.
quarterly_data.figure: FY March 2027 revenue +19%, adjusted OP +27%; DRAM sales +36%, logic foundry +38%, NAND +7%; WFE CY2026 raised to +15% (DRAM +25% - +30%)

quarterly_data.signal: Market position and POR pipeline: 2025 batch deposition market share rose 8 percentage points year-on-year to 49% (Gartner), and share of the batch ALD-compatible equipment segment reached 80%. In 3D NAND, 200-300-layer generation technology investment is expected to account for more than 80% of NAND-related equipment sales in FY March 2027, with PORs maintained and expanded for mini-batch deposition and single wafer treatment systems above 200 layers. In DRAM, D1C and D1D generation revenue is expected at roughly half of DRAM equipment revenue, with single wafer treatment PORs secured from the D1B generation onward and significant revenue growth expected; toward D0 and vertical channel transistor DRAM, more batch ALD adoption opportunities are expected. GAA sales were JPY 15 billion in FY March 2026 (below the JPY 20 billion forecast) and are forecast at JPY 20 billion for FY March 2027, with one first-generation 2-nanometer GAA POR already finalized and second-generation GAA PORs in competition. Advanced packaging revenue was JPY 3 billion and is expected at least at the same level. A U.S. demo center totaling JPY 20 billion opens in January 2027, and new land adjacent to the Tonami manufacturing center was acquired for production and R&D expansion.
quarterly_data.figure: Batch deposition share 49% (+8 points, 2025); batch ALD-compatible segment share 80%; GAA sales JPY 15 billion FY2026, JPY 20 billion forecast FY2027; U.S. demo center JPY 20 billion opening January 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2027 revenue of JPY 75.4 billion set a new record high for a single quarter, up 46% year-over-year, with adjusted operating income up 59% year-over-year to JPY 17.4 billion and gross profit margin of 40.7% (up 1.3 points QoQ on higher production utilization). By application, DRAM sales increased 158% year-over-year and logic foundry sales 82%, while NAND sales fell 34% year-over-year but climbed 84% sequentially. Sales to non-China manufacturers rose 75% year-over-year; sales to Chinese manufacturers slipped 3% year-over-year but rose 18% from the prior quarter, a recovery from the fourth-quarter low.

quarterly_data.signal: First quarter orders received totaled approximately JPY 140 billion, exceeding initial forecasts by about JPY 67 billion. The increase was particularly significant for DRAM for China, as well as for NAND sold to non-China and China, and this strong demand is expected to continue into the second quarter. Chinese demand is described as increasingly strong across major logic foundry, DRAM and NAND - not one-off, expected to continue at a minimum through this fiscal year and next, with medium and small emerging chip manufacturers also stronger and some companies announcing new factories.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 orders ~JPY 140 billion, ~JPY 67 billion above initial forecast

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year FY March 2027 guidance raised: revenue up 21% from the prior forecast to JPY 340 billion (+45% year-on-year), adjusted operating income up 42% to JPY 86 billion (+81% year-on-year), adjusted net income up 40% to JPY 60 billion; first half revised up 6% to JPY 161.0 billion (+37% YoY). Gross profit margin raised one point to 43% on product mix. Annual dividend raised JPY 18 to JPY 65 per share. CY2026 WFE growth outlook raised about 10 percentage points to over 25%, around $140 billion (from 15% growth and $120 billion-$125 billion), and CY2027 is expected to grow about 20% with possible further upside. The midterm revenue target of JPY 330 billion is now expected to be achieved in March 2027, two years ahead of schedule, with the 30%-or-higher adjusted operating margin target aimed for March 2028 via operating leverage, richer product mix (NAND CapEx strengthening), and pricing revisions. Non-China revenue is forecast to grow 49% (NAND +95%, DRAM +39%, logic and foundry +89%); China revenue +37% year-on-year with the share around 33%.
quarterly_data.figure: FY March 2027 revenue raised 21% to JPY 340 billion (+45% YoY); adjusted OP JPY 86 billion (+81% YoY); WFE CY2026 over 25% growth to ~$140 billion; midterm JPY 330 billion target hit two years ahead of schedule

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity utilization is expected at an average of 70%-80% in the first half and over 80% in the second half of March 2027, higher next fiscal year; production lead time is currently around eight months. Current capacity secures the JPY 340 billion revenue forecast, and capacity is being expanded for March 2028 and beyond: warehouse space at the Tonami plant is being converted to clean room, newly acquired land next to Tonami is being evaluated for rapid expansion, production engineer recruitment is ramping, and shifts (currently 1.5) can be increased. Monthly unit production capacity is targeted to reach 2.5 times the March 2025 level in 10 years. Investment timing has advanced about two years versus the WFE view at the start of the year; suppliers are also preparing capacity and are not currently a bottleneck.
quarterly_data.figure: Utilization 70%-80% H1, over 80% H2; lead time around eight months; monthly unit capacity targeted at 2.5 times the March 2025 level in 10 years

quarterly_data.signal: Growth catalysts: GAA sales were about JPY 5 billion in Q1 and are expected at over JPY 20 billion for FY March 2027. Advanced packaging revenue, JPY 6 billion in FY March 2026, is now expected at JPY 15 billion in FY March 2027 (Q1 was JPY 4.5 billion) - a significant upward revision from the JPY 6 billion prior plan, driven by both rising customer CapEx and additional POR wins for its film deposition technology. In NAND, demand-supply is not fully adjusted - memory players are allocating clean room to DRAM while NAND wafer output needs to increase - so greenfield NAND investments are expected to resume, which converts all of Kokusai's PORs to sales and is broadly favorable. In DRAM, the D1C transition is complete and D1D is progressing. NAND sales could approach record highs, and DRAM plus NAND plus advanced packaging support growth above WFE (targeting more than a 20% sales increase).

quarterly_data.signal: AI / HBM framing in the half-year report (2026-08-14): the memory market is leading semiconductor growth on AI and big-data demand, and the equipment market is expected to keep growing over the medium-to-long term on the aggressive DRAM-centric investment memory makers are making to break the HBM SHORTAGE caused by the explosive expansion of AI end-markets. 2022-2024 is described as a harsh down-cycle (memory price collapse, utilisation drop); 2025-2030 is framed as a structural growth phase driven by generative-AI infrastructure build-out, led by HBM and sub-2nm foundry rather than commodity products. The AI-accelerator and HBM demand surge is forcing the equipment market onto a single high-end track where marginal technology or adequate tools have no place; foreign vendors from the US, Japan and Netherlands still hold the largest shares but Korean localisation is rising and the company's tools are now in mass-production lines of major customers at home and abroad, with overseas sales rising (China semiconductor revenue KRW 63,346M in H1 2026 vs KRW 42,017M in H1 2025). Company cannot estimate market share because device makers' total orders are not observable.

quarterly_data.signal: AI test intensity is compounding because design margins are shrinking: higher data rates, lower latency and the requirement that AI fabrics be LOSSLESS mean customers 'can no longer guarantee anything by design' and must test in production too. A compute or switch tray has gone from tens to HUNDREDS of IC pinouts - more insertion points - tested at signal level (VNAs, oscilloscopes), at bit level (new portfolio) and at protocol/packet level (AI workload emulators). The move from monolithic chips to CHIPLET architectures adds interoperability emulation, and customers now ask for emulation environments that stress a chip while it exercises a model (thermal shutdown, all cores active at higher power and speed). The ecosystem is shifting from a homogeneous integrated vertical stack to a HETEROGENEOUS one - GPU/CPU/DPU mixes and a growing number of protocols at every layer of the stack - which broadens Keysight's addressable tail. The four wireline pillars (AI infrastructure scaling, speed transitions, silicon photonics, system-level emulation) all drove growth. Hyperscaler engagement (rooted in the Ixia acquisition ~5 years ago) is deepening as they integrate Keysight pre-silicon emulation and workload solutions into their development pipelines; hyperscalers plus the model companies are ~10% OF REVENUE DIRECTLY but drive large downstream influence, and many are building their own in-house silicon. Switch designers use Keysight emulators to validate network performance across AI workloads and protocols; interconnect manufacturers use high-fidelity analyzers to characterize high-speed backplanes for signal integrity and manufacturing yield.

quarterly_data.signal: NAND/DRAM scarcity is the defining constraint. CEO Wallace Kou: the AI super cycle has driven substantial HBM, DRAM, NAND and HDD price increases and 'mounting substrate and supply pressure,' and he expects the scarcity to persist 'likely until 2028 when new fabs come online.' DRAM and NAND now account for almost 56% of total BOM cost on a low-end smartphone, forcing OEMs to trim specifications; smartphone units are still expected down 10-15% in 2026. NAND makers are redirecting focus and CapEx to DRAM and HBM, deemphasising eMMC/UFS and exiting automotive - which hands share to Silicon Motion's module-maker customers and gives it stronger pricing power. Long-standing relationships let Silicon Motion secure NAND from multiple suppliers through the shortage, which management calls a significant and enduring differentiator.
quarterly_data.figure: NAND scarcity expected to persist until 2028; DRAM+NAND ~56% of low-end smartphone BOM; smartphone units -10% to -15% in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers entered commercial production in Q2 with TWO Tier 1 customers, with five additional Tier 1 customers expected to ramp in the second half. Management reaffirmed the target of 5-10% of total revenue coming from MonTitan exiting 2026. First customers are targeting the compute market with TLC NAND for AI platforms that use NAND for high-speed, low-latency storage dedicated to NEAR-GPU AND NEAR-CPU KV CACHE. TLC-based solutions are ramping ahead of QLC: early QLC shipments begin late 2026 but QLC only becomes meaningful late 2027 into 2028, gated by the availability and affordability of 2-terabit QLC dies. CFO Jason Tsai was explicit that the delay is a NAND-industry availability issue, not a controller issue.
quarterly_data.figure: 2 Tier 1 customers in production, 5 more ramping in H2; MonTitan targeted at 5-10% of revenue exiting 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Next-generation 4-nanometer PCIe Gen 6 MonTitan controller completes tape-out in August 2026, developed in close collaboration with customers and aimed at hyperscalers and cloud service providers. Multiple design wins are already secured with both flash makers and cloud service providers, and more than a dozen Tier 1 customers are waiting for samples. The architecture targets AI inference - management specifically cited NVIDIA's CMX architecture - plus multi-host operation under new AI workloads. Management expects the Gen 6 ramp to be 'much stronger and faster, bigger than our PCIe Gen 5 ramps' and set an initial target market share of at least 15-20%, with the controller becoming a significant growth driver in 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: 4nm PCIe Gen 6 tape-out August 2026; >12 Tier 1 customers awaiting samples; initial share target 15-20%; growth driver in 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Ferri for Automotive and Enterprise Boot Drive solutions MORE THAN DOUBLED sequentially and now represent nearly 30% of total revenue, up from 4% a year ago. These are controller-plus-NAND solutions, so ASPs are much higher than controller-only (and higher than MonTitan). The DRAM-less boot drive is the crown jewel: conventional DRAM-based boot drives for server CPUs stay with the NAND makers, but DPUs, TPUs, NPUs and switches favour DRAM-less designs for cost, security and performance - and NAND makers have no DRAM-less PCIe SSD controllers and little incentive to build them for a market where densities are only 256GB-512GB. A server rack can carry more than 30 or 40 boot drives, and per-drive capacity should rise. Management sees little competition from either NAND makers or module makers, and said Ferri plus Boot Drive reaching roughly one third of revenue in 2027 is 'certainly a possibility' given current backlog and pipeline.
quarterly_data.figure: Ferri + Boot Drive more than doubled QoQ to ~30% of revenue (from 4% a year ago); >30-40 boot drives per server rack

The 4-channel PCIe 5 controller introduced in Q4 of last year continues to ramp steadily in the mid- to high-end PC segment, and management still expects SSD average selling prices to rise through the year.

quarterly_data.signal: On NAND supply: 'we still able to get supply, but unfortunately supply not enough to what we need... We have supply, but supply still not enough what we need.' Phison met every NAND supplier at FMS last week and pitched that its purchases feed its own AI data-platform systems, not just module resale; it will not disclose how many LTAs it holds so competitors cannot ask for the same amounts. CEO expects the NAND shortage to continue into next year and beyond ('many year'); a top NAND-maker executive told him a new fab takes 4 years from investment to production, not 2. Downgrade-grade NAND supply is also shrinking structurally: 3D NAND yields now run 90-plus percent, with some wafers at 95% good die, so the cheap downgrade bin that used to feed consumer products is disappearing.

Demand is too strong, so price will keep rising but at a decelerating rate toward saturation, at which point suppliers start choosing whom to ship. On demand structure: systems have cut DRAM content ('a lot of systems, they cut half of the DRAM') but nobody cuts storage - inference needs storage, 'storage is money' - and aiDAPTIV uses flash to complement DRAM.

quarterly_data.signal: CALL — THE FIBER-CONTENT-PER-GPU FRAMEWORK (the definitive supply-side math for optical in AI factories). Base case: enterprise grows at the rate GPUs grow; THREE drivers add on top. (1) CLUSTER SIZE: clusters ABOVE ~130,000 GPUs exceed a 512-radix switch's two-layer span and need a THIRD OPTICAL LAYER -> ~50% MORE CONTENT PER GPU for very large clusters. (2) BANDWIDTH (doubles ~every 2 years): Hopper -> Blackwell kept 100G SerDes so fibers went 8 -> 16 per GPU (content DOUBLED); the RUBIN era jumps SerDes to 200G with lane count flat -> NEUTRAL; Feynman (~2029-30): fibers double again IF SerDes stays 200G, neutral if 400G arrives (BiDi/WDM could offset) — Springboard conservatively assumes NEUTRAL. (3) SCALE-UP, today 100% COPPER: Vera Rubin Ultra NVL576 is a HYBRID step — copper inside each 72-GPU rack, DIRECT OPTICAL rack-to-rack. Bracketing a full-optical scale-up: 14.4 Tbps scale-up / 200G = 72 lanes x 2 fibers = 144, plus scale-out 1.6 Tbps / 200G = 16 fibers -> 160 FIBERS PER GPU = 10x today's 16-fiber scale-out-only content (reality lands between; % of optical ports is confidential). COMBINED: optical content per GPU +1.3-1.5x BY 2028 and 'much, much higher' toward 2030. Status: Q2 enterprise strength is 'ALL JUST SCALE-OUT — we are not yet seeing scale-up or photonics in our results'; orders accelerating; 'if we could make more, we could sell more.'
quarterly_data.figure: Content/GPU drivers: 3rd optical layer >130k GPUs (+50%); Blackwell 16 fibers; full-optical scale-up = 160 fibers/GPU (10x); +1.3-1.5x by 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CALL — PHOTONICS: A $10B MAP BY 2030, AND THE LTA MODEL: Corning's new PHOTONICS Market-Access Platform targets $10 BILLION of revenue by 2030 — passive photonics INSIDE THE BOX (FAU harnesses and everything that moves/manages light between the faceplate and the silicon-photonics optical engine) for CPO/NPO, where Corning historically had ZERO content; likely starts with scale-out, and optical SCALE-UP supercharges it; the plan is built on 'assumptions and discussions AND AGREEMENTS with customers.' Despite industry chatter on scale-up timing, 'NO CHANGES to our fundamental belief... inside the real ecosystem there is much less drama than what it looks like from outside.' Business model: long-term agreements (Amazon multi-billion, NVIDIA, Meta up-to-$6B, Apple) will be 'the LION'S SHARE of our optical business' — every major capacity expansion is underpinned by risk/reward-sharing LTAs; profitability comes from innovation value-share, not bare-fiber pricing (optical NI +77% to a record 21% margin). Springboard math: run rate $20B by end-2026 (Q3 guide may hit it a QUARTER EARLY) -> $30B (2028) -> $40B (2030), 19% CAGR; high-confidence variant $27B/$35B; biggest risk-adjustment between the two = SCALE-UP TIMING. Because near and co-packaged optics are built on a common photonic IC - an EIC bonded to a PIC with a micro-optic and a fiber-attached unit - and differ mainly in that NPO is bonded to the board while CPO sits within the package (plus SerDes architecture differences), GF expects to benefit regardless of which form factor customers adopt. Many customers are pursuing both, with NPO ramping sooner. Breen attributed the sudden industry interest in NPO to SerDes synergies that make the system transition smaller than a jump straight to full CPO, and expects pluggables, NPO and CPO all to coexist in the data center.

quarterly_data.signal: Silicon germanium is OVERSUBSCRIBED THROUGHOUT 2027 and, notably, GF's SiGe business is LARGER THAN ITS SILICON PHOTONICS BUSINESS TODAY. GF secured multiple new SiGe TIA and driver design wins across networking customers in the quarter. The growth has two compounding drivers: the shift to optical networking itself, and the fact that what could previously be done in CMOS at 50-gig and 100-gig per lane cannot be done at 200-gig and definitely not at 400-gig per lane, forcing transimpedance amplifiers and increasingly the drivers out into high-performance analog processes like SiGe. High-performance analog also appears in near and co-packaged optics depending on architecture. GF is expanding SiGe capacity at Burlington, Vermont and qualifying 300-millimeter SiGe in Singapore for additional capacity, better economics and higher fT/fMAX performance. The SiGe lineage traces to IBM Microelectronics, which invented SiGe and is part of GF today.

quarterly_data.signal: GF launched Quantum Technology Solutions in May 2026, a dedicated team aimed at taking the quantum industry from prototypes to high-volume production. The strategy is qubit-agnostic across superconducting, trapped ion, photonic, topological and spin modalities, using the FDX platform as a cryogenic CMOS foundation and extending advanced packaging into the cryogenic regime for 3D heterogeneous integration. GF is working with 8 of the world's leading quantum computing players including PsiQuantum, Quantinuum and Quantum Motion plus endorsements from the quantum arms of large hyperscalers, and has already begun 4 new customer-specific engagements in the three months since launch. The effort is anchored by an expected $375 MILLION grant from the U.S. Department of Commerce. Over the next 1 to 3 years quantum revenue comes largely through engineering engagements booked in technology services, with manufacturing-services revenue ramping toward the end of the decade. Several quantum players are working on the photonics side of their solutions, which maps directly onto GF's silicon photonics roadmap.

quarterly_data.signal: IP, software and custom silicon: GF completed the acquisition of the Synopsys ARC processor IP Solutions business in June, adding CPU, DSP, NPU and RISC-V technologies, a software development toolkit and application-specific processor design capability - over 150 patents, 300 existing customers and 400 R&D engineers. Critically, MACOM says it will NOT build or supply optical engines - in Data Center it is a chip supplier, not a multichip assembly or module supplier. It describes the architectural evolution as pluggable transceivers with DSPs, to LPO platforms that remove the DSP, morphing into smaller package-less NPO platforms; those architectures still need drivers and TIAs, but with much higher density - smaller parts, more channels, lower power, and varied form factors using wire bonds, bumped devices or flip chip, plus through-silicon-via options. Because these solutions are specific to the architectures hyperscalers are driving, the design wins come directly to MACOM. Related applications include LPO and LRO on single mode or multimode.

quarterly_data.signal: MARKET / ROADMAP DATA POINTS: 800G transceiver INDUSTRY volume went from ~20 MILLION UNITS/YEAR two years ago to ~90 MILLION UNITS/YEAR this year — the industry entered the year forecasting 50M units and Semtech is 'now hearing the number 80, 90 million'; 800G bookings are still INCREASING (not decreasing), and 800G and 1.6T both have 'a really very healthy runway over the next two years'. 3.2T TIMING: design window starts opening in ~12 MONTHS, EARLY MOVERS ~18 MONTHS OUT, MEANINGFUL DEPLOYMENT IN ~2 YEARS (i.e. H2 CY2028) — that is the cut-in for Semtech's content step-up, and above 200G/lane is where TIA + photodiode CO-OPTIMIZATION becomes necessary. MPO/NPO called a strong trend driven by BANDWIDTH-DENSITY limits against fixed shoreline: Semtech is engaged on '10, 15 DIFFERENT PROGRAMS' with module manufacturers, some tied directly to end customers, as a leading supplier of TIA ARRAYS and (linearized) LASER ARRAYS; higher density tightens element spacing and crosstalk, changing packaging requirements. LPO has generated meaningful revenue since Q1 FY2027 and is growing moderately, but its bigger effect is PROVING THE LINEAR ARCHITECTURE, which now carries into MPO, XPO and 'some form of CPO'. Stated R&D priority: lasers, photodiodes, drivers and TIAs for 3.2T coherent light, XPO, MPO and CPO applications. Analyst day 10-15-2026 (San Jose) will publish TAM, share and the multi-year model.

Significant design uptick for ADI protection and 800V-to-intermediate conversion technology delivering 20 kW at industry-leading power density exceeding 2.5 kW per cubic inch, as the industry transitions to 800V DC power distribution. At the intermediate-to-core conversion layer - called ONE OF THE FASTEST AND LARGEST GROWING ANALOG OPPORTUNITIES IN THE AI ERA - ADI combines advanced power conversion, intelligent system control and real-time telemetry for next-generation processors operating at 6,000 A and sub-1V. Framing on efficiency: a 97% converter loses roughly 50% more energy as heat than a 98% one, compounding into cooling infrastructure and opex.

In large-scale AI deployments the architecture reduces compute power consumption and temperature by approximately 10%-15%, equating to roughly $30 MILLION IN ANNUAL SAVINGS IN A 1 GW DATA CENTER. Cash and short-term investments fell to $2.3B on the close; net leverage ratio now 0.9.

quarterly_data.signal: GRID-TO-CHIP strategy: data center capacity is now measured in GIGAWATTS rather than FLOPS/TOPS and POWER AVAILABILITY HAS BECOME THE PRIMARY CONSTRAINT TO FURTHER AI PROGRESS. ADI supplies grid monitoring (real-time voltage, current, power quality, system health) to utilities, energy operators and infrastructure providers, plus battery management for energy storage - one of the grid's fastest-growing sectors. To accelerate time-to-power, hyperscalers are increasingly exploring DEDICATED MICROGRIDS, opening additional growth avenues that augment ADI's $500M+ energy business (inflected in 2025, accelerating in 2026). ADI now spans the entire electricity value chain: generation, transmission, storage, distribution, rack power and ultimately processor power delivery - 'essentially the vascular system of the data center.'

quarterly_data.signal: 2030 SAM RESET: ADI's current assessment is that its 2030 data center AND energy SAM has MORE THAN DOUBLED versus what it envisioned just one year ago - driven not simply by higher AI infrastructure CapEx but by new markets and architectures requiring ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE MORE ANALOG CONTENT delivered via higher-value solutions. Supporting math from the call: ~100 GW equivalent of data center infrastructure is expected to be built between now and 2031, with EACH GIGAWATT generating a $1B-$1.5B analog SAM. Runway seen extending to at least 2030 for strong double-digit data center growth; the ~$0.5B energy business is expected to DOUBLE by the end of the decade. ADI is contemplating long-term company growth above the 5%-7% model set at its 2021 investor day.

On the 110kW power shelf and other new product cycles Delta believes its market share remains high because it engages customers earliest, and the fast generational churn of AI power architecture favors its engineering resources; it declined to quantify share for the Rubin-linked 110kW PSU but asserts market leadership. A solid-state transformer (an energy gateway, not a one-for-one transformer replacement) has its first trial customers in smaller data centers, and a first small fuel-cell line starts by year-end with the first volume line planned next year, with units at Taipower and another test site performing well.

quarterly_data.signal: Component supply is tight across the board: lead times are stretching and MOSFETs in particular are short, though Delta's purchasing scale and supplier relationships keep demand largely fulfilled. Memory was the hardest hit - one business unit could not secure memory volumes at workable prices, so it switched designs to second sources and expects H2 shipments to normalize and catch up the backlog without a loss. Management does not expect power semiconductors to repeat memory's shortage dynamics - the two situations differ a lot - but notes power-semi supply is cyclical because capacity investment takes long. On wide-bandgap devices (silicon carbide, gallium nitride) Delta works early and closely with the most important suppliers, keeps talking with them continuously and gets early access to new products, but will not disclose any agreements; it is also broadening its supply chain, including Taiwanese supplier options. Supplier price increases will be negotiated and passed to customers where the business model allows, with a timing lag.

Electrification revenue $5.2 billion (+19% comparable), Operational EBITA +26% to $1.3 billion at a record 24.9% margin. Customer mix unchanged (hyperscalers vs colocation similar) — 'the whole segment is running faster'; significant data-center wins also in Europe and Asia this quarter. Backlog deliveries extend beyond 2027 into 2028, including some data centers. Management: gained market share in data centers at least since Q1; strong position in medium-voltage UPS.
quarterly_data.figure: Electrification orders +58% to above $7 billion (first time); data-center orders +triple digits; EL backlog $13.7 billion (+59%); group backlog $30 billion; book-to-bill 1.39

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 guidance RAISED: comparable revenue growth now expected at low double-digit to low teens (from high-single-to-low-double); Operational EBITA margin to improve from 2025 even excluding the Q1 real-estate gain. Q3 guide: low to mid-teens comparable revenue growth with sequential margin improvement (Electrification revenue growth at least similar to Q2 with margin improving from 24.9%; Motion mid-to-high single digit; Automation mid-single digit). Free cash flow to improve from 2025's $4.6 billion. Pricing +~2% in the quarter, strongest in the Americas; price-cost gap to be more than compensated by year-end.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 comparable revenue growth raised to low double-digit to low teens; Q3 low to mid-teens; FCF to improve from $4.6 billion

quarterly_data.signal: 800V DC data centers: 'We have ZERO order in the backlog for 800 volt DC data centers. Nobody has, because there is waiting for the availability of components from NVIDIA and the like.' Commercial impact seen from late 2027 or 2028 onwards; ABB building the complete 800V DC portfolio now — already a leading player in DC switches, breakers and components, expects the new architecture to shift more content to medium voltage, boosting its medium-voltage UPS. Heavy R&D allocation plus the announced acquisition of Advantics (France — DC technology, silicon carbide technology, joining Electrification for DC and data center). Dedicated DC-topic webcast announced for September 24.
quarterly_data.figure: Zero 800V DC orders in backlog industry-wide; commercial opportunity late 2027/2028; Advantics acquisition adds DC/SiC technology

quarterly_data.signal: Motion orders reached $2.6 billion (+20% comparable), rising sequentially against the usual seasonal trend, with strength in grid stabilization (industry-leading synchronous condensers), rail, marine, mining, HVAC for commercial buildings and DATA CENTER COOLING. ABB positions as the COMPONENT PROVIDER to the cooling industry: 'We are partnering with all of the major cooling companies in the world who delivers those air cooling or large chiller units that sits in the data centers today' — supplying drives and motors, and in liquid cooling the pumps that push liquid to the rack. Motion revenue $2.2 billion (+4%); margin 18.5% (-130bps: Gamesa Electric dilution ~70bps, High Power inefficiencies to resolve in H2).
quarterly_data.figure: Motion orders $2.6 billion (+20%); revenue $2.2 billion (+4%); margin 18.5%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity is the governor of order intake: 'We do not take orders where we aren't fully committed that we can deliver on time.' Guidance raised because capacity from previous years' investments is now coming online with the expected benefits; multi-year CapEx build-out across the US, China and India, plus a newly announced $200 million expansion and additional CapEx into Europe. Continuous expansion 'especially in Electrification, every unit that we have with more square meter, more Robotics, more Automation and more people'. Lead times unchanged — order strength reflects real demand, not lead-time extension or pre-buying.
quarterly_data.figure: $200 million additional European capacity CapEx announced; capacity additions in US, China, India

quarterly_data.signal: Announced offer to acquire Rotork, a leading independent manufacturer of actuators (electric actuators more than half of sales), at GBP 5.03 per share — about $5.5 billion in USD terms (EV/sales ~5.3x, EV/EBITDA ~19.5x 2025, mid-teens with synergies). Rotork 2025 revenue GBP 777 million at a 24.6% adjusted operating margin; would add ~3% to ABB revenues and ~12% to Automation revenues, run as a separate division. Actuators are also needed in data-center cooling applications and nuclear power. Close expected H1 2027. Two smaller deals: Specialtrasfo (medium-voltage transformers, Italy) and Hoglund (marine automation).
quarterly_data.figure: Rotork offer GBP 5.03/share (~$5.5 billion); Rotork 2025 revenue GBP 777 million, 24.6% margin

quarterly_data.signal: RECORD BACKLOG OF $53 BILLION - and the big work is not in it yet. Duke Austin: 'The record backlog we reported reflects the demand in front of us, but we're still in the early stages. The larger programs across the utility generation and technology load center markets are ahead of us, and we expect them to stack in the years to come.' The 765 kV corridors, 345 kV and 500 kV transmission are still in engineering ('We're not in backlog on any of the bigger work yet'), and about 95% of the generation work is not in backlog either. He expects record backlog again in the third quarter and probably the fourth. Book-to-burn will be lumpy: 1:1 to 1:2 in ordinary quarters, 1:5 to 1:6 in quarters when big chunks of projects land (the 765 kV work brought in last quarter was that kind of boost) - 'lower lows and higher highs all the way through'. A large share of the technology work never touches backlog at all: MEP crews can 'book and bill $300 million on a site in a quarter' against an MSA and 'you never see it show up in backlog'. CFO Jayshree Desai on data-center backlog discipline: only items with limited notices to proceed go in, 'we don't put the rest in until the project is a confirmed go.'

quarterly_data.signal: Craft labour is NOT the binding constraint today - Duke Austin: 'We're nowhere near capacity.' More than 85,000 employees; roughly 15,500 people added over the past year, well over 7,000 of them organic with a significant portion in Q2; Quanta spends about $250 million a year on training. It takes about four years to make a craftsman and a journeyman, and he sees no oversupply of craft-skilled labour in the near future. Labour is fungible across segments - electricians and underground crews move between data-center work, industrial and gas compression work and T&D - which is where the acquisition synergies show up. Customers are securing craft as far out as their five- to seven-year capital plans, with 'decade-plus type arrangements out there'. Margin follows that utilisation: the electric segment can operate at 10% to 12% on the utility side, with 12% the utmost 'when you stack in large transmission and all aspects at once', and Duke sees room for further margin improvement in the second half.

quarterly_data.signal: The stacking has not started. quarterly_data.signal: VERTICAL INTEGRATION INTO CRITICAL-PATH EQUIPMENT. Duke Austin, asked where else he would add manufacturing after transformers and a utility pole company: 'We did the breaker deal with HICO. I thought that was a critical path for us and the high-voltage breakers are very difficult to get. You've seen us build them and partner.' The rule he states: 'Anywhere there's a critical path that we think we can invest capital to move it forward, that's what you've seen us do... we're taking advantage of areas where there's underinvestment', and those vertical supply-chain investments are 'showing up in synergies'. He will stay selective - EBOS companies are explicitly not a focus. The other leg is integrated fabrication: about seven million square feet of fabrication space, plus roughly 0.5 million square feet added with the recent acquisitions, with VDC (virtual design and construction) engineering in front of it so modules are designed for constructability. Done collaboratively with the client it takes total installed cost down significantly and de-risks logistics; the Phalcon acquisition puts that capacity in the Northeast, close to where the work is.

quarterly_data.signal: Technology is now 15% to 20% of Quanta's business - 'a spectrum from chips to everything, not just data centers' - grown to that share over the last two years off the Cupertino Electric platform, and Duke Austin frames it as a second TAM 'every bit as big as our utility TAM'. Quanta sells direct to the hyperscalers and to the larger technology customers, and can self-perform 'call it 80% of what a data center build is, maybe 90%', taking balance-of-plant scope and full-scale data-center opportunities on more and more sites; it is also picking up work at semiconductor plants, at manufacturing and medical facilities, and at Tesla. The pitch is speed and certainty: 'Technology is trying to move as fast as possible. Utilities are working to protect the ratepayer, and Quanta sits in the middle of that nexus.' On state-level data-center moratoriums (New York): immaterial - 'nothing really gets built there' - and these are eight- to ten-year developments, not one-year builds, with multiyear projects extending well beyond 2030.
quarterly_data.figure: Technology = 15% to 20% of the business; Quanta can self-perform 80% to 90% of a data-center build

quarterly_data.signal: WHERE THE BOTTLENECK ACTUALLY IS: interconnection and utility-scale generation, not Quanta's labour. Duke Austin: 'I'm not sure people understand that nexus and how difficult it is to interconnect to the grid and how much we're right in the middle of that interconnection', pointing at 'the queues on the utility side of substations, all the substations that are out there. We're right in the middle of that.' 'It takes generation and substations to get to the queue', and many data centers want to connect back to the grid at some point, which utilities do better than anyone. On generation he says it is 'technically difficult to have capacity to build combined cycles at the levels and speed desired', and that orders for engines placed today often carry a five- to six-year lead time - which he reads as evidence of how long this build lasts. Quanta does EPC on generation both in front of the meter and behind the meter, small engines through big engines, but will not take the risk on the combined-cycle side and some single-cycle engines without the contract terms it needs; some utilities are attempting to self-perform gas generation RFPs because of inadequate resources, which he has seen fail before.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (engine orders placed today carry a five- to six-year lead time; substation interconnection queue is the constraint)

quarterly_data.signal: REGULATORY UNLOCK FOR LARGE LOADS moving far faster than expected. FERC in June ordered EVERY RTO to justify (or revise) how its tariff provides just and reasonable interconnection of LARGE LOADS, and directed PJM to explain why co-located transmission services cannot be made available more quickly; FERC is also willing to study GENERATION AND LOAD TOGETHER AT A COMMON POINT OF INTERCONNECTION, which Constellation has advocated. PJM released proposals for the RELIABILITY BACKSTOP PROCUREMENT (RBP) and INTERIM RESOURCE ADEQUACY SERVICE (IRAS), set a target of 6.8 GW for the RBP, and is running a BILATERAL MATCHMAKING process to pair customers with new supply and shrink the centrally procured amount; the RBP auction is proposed for this fall with RESULTS BY YEAR-END. Co-location rule clarity is now expected in Q1-Q2 2027 (PJM response due ~November 2026, FERC order Q1-Q2 2027) versus PJM's earlier 2029 target. Separately Constellation is urging the EPA to exclude FERC-tariff-directed curtailments from the 50-HOUR ANNUAL LIMIT on data-center BACKUP GENERATORS, which management says may be the most effective way to cover the few peak hours

quarterly_data.signal: CONTRACTED AI/DATA-CENTER LOAD CROSSES 17 GW. Four large-load projects were signed in the quarter alone: three projects in Alabama where Alabama Power added approximately 3 GW, plus a Georgia Power 3.2 GW, 25-year electric service contract with OpenAI at its newly announced site near Savannah, Georgia. Combined, those four projects represent 6 GW of newly contracted customer load, and together with agreements previously signed they bring total contracted large load agreements across Southern's electric subsidiaries to over 17 GW by the mid-2030s. CEO Christopher Womack framed the vertically integrated, state-regulated model (one-stop shop across generation, transmission and distribution) as the differentiator winning hyperscaler and data-center developer business in the Southeast.
quarterly_data.figure: 6 GW newly contracted in Q2 (Alabama ~3 GW + Georgia Power/OpenAI 3.2 GW); total contracted large load over 17 GW by mid-2030s

quarterly_data.signal: PROSPECTIVE LARGE-LOAD PIPELINE STILL ABOVE 75 GW, WITH 8 GW IN LATE-STAGE NEGOTIATION. Womack: new projects continue to be added to the prospective pipeline of large industrial and data-center projects, 'which remains well above 75 GW.' Beyond the 17 GW already contracted there are an additional 8 GW of projects in late stages, including 3 GW projected to be finalized in the near term; CFO David Poroch said those contracts are likely to go into 2028 and beyond, with a couple of them initiating their ramp-up in 2028 and running into the next decade. Womack also noted momentum migrating west, with 100 MW projects already succeeding in Mississippi and increasing activity there and in Alabama.
quarterly_data.figure: Prospective pipeline well above 75 GW; 8 GW late-stage of which 3 GW near-term; 100 MW projects in Mississippi

quarterly_data.signal: DATA-CENTER LOAD ACTUALLY ON THE SYSTEM IS COMPOUNDING FAST. System-wide data-center load now exceeds 1.2 GW, an increase of more than 500 megawatts over the prior year, and Poroch noted the company 'crossed over the 1,000 MW line this particular quarter.' Data-center usage was 55% higher than Q2 2025 and is up 49% year to date, primarily due to accelerating load ramps from large-load customers. That pulled weather-normal commercial sales up 7.4% in Q2 (+6% year to date) and total weather-normal retail electricity sales up 2.3% in the first half - the highest retail sales growth through June in nearly two decades. Q2 adjusted EPS was $1.13, up $0.21 versus Q2 2025 and $0.13 above the company's own estimate; first-half adjusted EPS was $2.46.
quarterly_data.figure: Data-center load >1.2 GW (+500 MW YoY); data-center usage +55% YoY in Q2, +49% YTD; commercial sales +7.4% Q2; Q2 adjusted EPS $1.13

quarterly_data.signal: GUIDANCE RAISED TO THE TOP OF THE RANGE ON LOAD GROWTH. Management now projects full-year 2026 adjusted earnings to be near or at the top of the $4.50-$4.60 adjusted EPS guidance range, with a Q3 adjusted EPS estimate of $1.50 per share, and reiterated the goal of being toward the top half of the long-term earnings trajectory. Drivers named were increased usage and customer growth, higher AFUDC from ongoing construction projects, higher earnings from equity-method investments, and contributions from Southern Company Gas and PowerSecure, where distributed, backup and bridge power solutions markets for data centers continue to expand.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance $4.50-$4.60, now expected near or at the top; Q3 estimate $1.50

quarterly_data.signal: GENERATION BUILDOUT FOR AI LOAD - 10 GW APPROVED AND GEORGIA ALREADY OVERSUBSCRIBED. Over the past several years Southern has secured regulatory approvals for 10 GW of new company-owned generation resources, including thermal, battery and solar, as well as hundreds of miles of new transmission lines. The first two of several battery sites are in service, and work on three combustion turbines at Plant Yates is advancing toward completion in the coming quarters. Poroch said the company is 'about 1 GW or 2 away from... selling out the capacity that we had approved in Georgia last year', and Womack added that 'the OpenAI contract in Georgia pushes us beyond our recently approved capacity by right around 1 GW' - i.e. the signed AI load has already outrun approved supply.
quarterly_data.figure: 10 GW of new company-owned generation approved (thermal/battery/solar) + hundreds of miles of transmission; Georgia capacity ~1 GW oversubscribed after the OpenAI contract

quarterly_data.signal: OPEN RFPs AT ALABAMA POWER AND GEORGIA POWER ARE INCREMENTAL CAPITAL NOT YET IN THE PLAN. Ongoing RFPs at both utilities are procuring additional generation for the early 2030s. Poroch was explicit that 'there is not placeholders in our capital plan... the RFPs that are open in Alabama, the RFPs that are open in Georgia, none of that is contemplated in our capital forecast at the moment,' and gave a sizing rule of thumb of 'about $2 billion or so, a little bit above maybe related to 1 GW of new generating capacity.' Timeline: selections known by year end 2026, a certification process running through much of 2027 with clarity in the latter part of 2027, spend feathering in around 2028, and the generation coming online in the 2030-2031 timeline. Alabama runs a near-parallel schedule.
quarterly_data.figure: Capital rule of thumb ~$2B per 1 GW of new generating capacity; RFP selections by year-end 2026, certification through 2027, generation online 2030-2031

quarterly_data.signal: HOW THE AI-LOAD CONTRACTS ARE CREDIT-PROTECTED - ABOUT $21 BILLION OF COLLATERAL BEHIND 17 GW. The large-load contracting framework has four pillars: long-term contracts (the OpenAI contract is 25 years), minimum bills covering at least 100% of the incremental cost to serve, default/termination provisions, and default payments tied to collateral. Poroch said forms of collateral include parent guarantees, lines of credit and surety bonds depending on counterparty credit quality, with the aim of a collateral portfolio equivalent to about A- or better. He initially cited '$20.8 billion of collateral... in the aggregate on full ramp' and then clarified that this refers to the entire portfolio: 'the whole portfolio of the 17 GW, we got about $21 billion of collateral.' Minimum bills effectively decouple revenue from actual customer ramp rates, which Womack said often differ from what was predicted at project approval.
quarterly_data.figure: About $21 billion of collateral in aggregate at full ramp across the 17 GW contracted portfolio; minimum bills cover 100% of incremental cost to serve

quarterly_data.signal: FIRST FLEXIBLE-DEMAND DATA CENTER: 1 GW OF DEMAND RESPONSE AT THE OPENAI SITE. The Savannah site features 1 GW of flexible demand response, and Womack confirmed this is the first time Southern has done that for a data center. Poroch said demand-response flexibility 'does enter into all those conversations' and is possible because the three electric jurisdictions are not limited to a tariff and can negotiate bilateral contracts that price hyperscaler flexibility. Womack said technical requirements - how a hyperscaler's operations affect the system and the grid, and whether it can be more than 'just a taker' - are raised very early in every hyperscaler conversation, and that peak shaving from this resource benefits the whole system.
quarterly_data.figure: 1 GW of flexible demand response at the OpenAI Savannah site - Southern's first for a data center

quarterly_data.signal: NEW NUCLEAR: HYPERSCALERS BEING ASKED TO SHARE AP1000 COST-OVERRUN RISK. Womack said the country needs more nuclear units in operation particularly in the mid-2030s, credited the administration for regulatory actions and for convening groups around long-lead-time items, but stated plainly that 'Southern Company is not going to be next' on a new nuclear build. Asked whether hyperscalers are willing to absorb cost overruns above budgeted amounts for AP1000s, he said he did not want to get ahead of a firm conclusion but 'yes, we are having conversations with them in terms of what role they can play.'

Poroch added that conversations with both current and new Southern Power counterparties are 'proving to be very fruitful', covering repricing of expiring contracts into the next decade plus the previously announced uprate/brownfield opportunities, with an update expected later in the year; the business will not 'build something and see who shows up.'

quarterly_data.signal: A RARE DOWNWARD REVISION TO A DATA-CENTER PIPELINE — AND WHY IT MATTERS: Exelon's data-center growth pipeline now shows a combined 36 GIGAWATTS, DOWN ROUGHLY 11 GW FROM THE 43 GW previously cited. CFO Jeanne Jones attributes the cut not to demand weakness but to Exelon's own screening discipline: it developed TRANSMISSION SECURITY AGREEMENTS (TSAs) that 'never existed in our regions', and its cluster process now requires a customer to sign a TSA and, importantly, 'PUT UP COLLATERAL BEHIND THAT'. The result: 'what this update reflects is we have now WEEDED OUT SPECULATIVE PROJECTS, and it gives us proactive insight into what is real.' Exelon says it has deliberately kept capex increases consistent with historical levels and only committed capital that was 'certain and durable', alongside its stance on CO-LOCATION and fair cost allocation to shield existing customers from infrastructure costs. This is a useful reality-check datapoint on how much of the headline AI interconnection queue is firm versus speculative.
quarterly_data.figure: Data-centre pipeline cut 43 GW -> 36 GW after TSA + COLLATERAL requirements weeded out speculative projects

Announced with the results: a global leader in optical and photonics technologies selected Veeco's Lumina+ MOCVD system to fabricate indium phosphide lasers for the datacom industry; Lumina+ offers the largest batch size in the MOCVD industry, best-in-class throughput, lowest cost per wafer, and can deposit high-quality epitaxial layers on InP wafers of any size. Veeco is also a market leader in WaferEtch/WaferStorm wet processing and in the SPECTOR ion beam deposition tool used for the critical laser facet coating step, where its IBD is differentiated as the industry moves to higher-power lasers with stricter film specifications. Management framed the driver as the industry 'overcoming the copper wall,' with hyperscalers advancing EML pluggables, silicon photonics pluggables and the longer-term near-package and co-packaged optics architectures - all of which rely increasingly on InP lasers.
